# Fwdpod

> Fwdpod adds pre-vetted senior AI engineers from India to enterprise teams: one specialist or a full AI pod of 4–6 engineers, hourly or full-time, to build and run AI agents, RAG systems, voice AI and LLMOps.

## Pods

- [Our Solutions](https://fwdpod.com/our-solutions): Senior AI engineers from India to build and run every layer of your AI stack: agents, RAG, models, data, compliance and LLMOps. One specialist or a full pod.
- [Case studies](https://fwdpod.com/case-studies): Recent AI pods in production: a Compliance AI Pod for a financial brokerage, an Agent Development Pod for a logistics network and a Voice AI Pod for healthcare services, each with the problem, what was built, time to live and team size.
- [How we work](https://fwdpod.com/how-we-work): The principles behind every engagement, the four steps from first call to start (scope, shortlist, interview, start), how quality is kept high, and how your environment, IP and NDAs are handled.

## Solutions

- [Agents and applications](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/ai-agents): AI agents and workflow automation across ERP, CRM and service desk, built by senior AI engineers from India. One specialist or an Agent Development Pod.
- [Voice AI](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/voice-ai): Real-time voice agents for support, scheduling and intake, connected to your phone system. Built by a Voice AI Pod of senior AI engineers from India.
- [Context and knowledge](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/rag): RAG systems and enterprise search that answer correctly about your business, with permission-aware answers. Built by senior AI engineers from India.
- [Models](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/models): Model selection, fine-tuning, private deployment and inference tuning for speed and cost. Senior ML engineers from India, as specialists or a Custom Pod.
- [Data](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/data-annotation): Data pipelines, annotation and labelling at scale, evaluation datasets and RLHF. Clean, labelled data your AI can learn from and be tested against.
- [Trust and compliance](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/ai-compliance): Guardrails, privacy filters, audit logs and red-team testing, so your risk, legal and audit teams can sign off your AI. A Compliance AI Pod from India.
- [Operations (LLMOps)](https://fwdpod.com/solutions/llmops): Deployment, monitoring, incident response and cost control for AI in production. An LLMOps Pod of senior engineers from India on a monthly retainer.

## Resources

- [Book a 30-minute call](https://fwdpod.com/configure): Request a call about the roles or the outcome you need. Fwdpod sends matched profiles or a pod plan within 48 hours.
- [How to engage](https://fwdpod.com/how-to-engage): Add one AI specialist or a full AI pod, hourly or full-time. Start with a paid pilot on one use case, then grow into a dedicated team.
- [Security](https://fwdpod.com/security): Your code, your data, your control. Clear answers on how we keep your work safe.
- [About](https://fwdpod.com/about): Senior AI engineers from India inside enterprise teams. Backed by Nextdot since 2018, with engineers trained at our Jamshedpur AI Capability Center.
- [Contact Us](https://fwdpod.com/contact): Send Fwdpod a message about AI engineers, AI pods or how engagements work, or email contact.fwdpod@gmail.com.

## Insights

- [What Is a Forward Deployed Engineer? The 2026 Definition](https://fwdpod.com/insights/what-is-a-forward-deployed-engineer): The 2026 definition of the forward deployed engineer role: its origin at Palantir, what FDEs do day to day, the skills the AI labs hire for, and how the forward deployed AI engineer variant differs.
- [What Is an AI Pod? How a Small Cross-Functional Team Ships AI Faster Than a Hire-and-Build Team](https://fwdpod.com/insights/what-is-an-ai-pod): What an AI pod is: a small cross-functional team that owns one AI outcome end to end, where the model comes from, how it differs from a generic dev team, how pods are engaged, and when a pod is the wrong choice.
- [How to Hire AI Engineers in 2026: Roles, Screening, Red Flags](https://fwdpod.com/insights/how-to-hire-ai-engineers): How to hire AI engineers: how the role differs from ML engineer and data scientist, what to define before the job ad, sourcing including India, a four-stage screen built on a RAG and evals take-home, interview questions, red flags and timelines.
- [AI Development Engagement Models Explained: Who Carries the Risk, and When Each One Fits](https://fwdpod.com/insights/ai-engagement-models-explained): Seven ways to buy AI engineering — time and materials, fixed scope, dedicated and shared pods, staff augmentation, forward deployed engineers, build-operate-transfer and outcome-based — with who carries the overrun risk in each and the contract clauses to read twice.
- [How Enterprises Buy AI Engineering Capacity in 2026](https://fwdpod.com/insights/how-enterprises-buy-ai-engineering-capacity): The six channels enterprises buy AI engineering through, what an AI implementation partner owns versus what stays in-house, and the eight-step procurement path from intake through security review, MSA, DPA and IP terms to a scoped pilot.
- [Who Owns the IP When You Outsource AI Development? A Plain-English Guide](https://fwdpod.com/insights/ip-ownership-offshore-ai): Default copyright ownership of outsourced AI work in the US, UK and India, the AI assets a contract must name beyond code — prompts, weights, datasets, eval sets, embeddings — and a twelve-point assignment checklist including India's Section 19 term and territory rules.
- [What Is MCP? The Model Context Protocol Explained for Enterprise Buyers](https://fwdpod.com/insights/what-is-mcp): What the Model Context Protocol is: hosts, clients and servers, the tools, resources and prompts a server exposes, stdio and Streamable HTTP transports, the stateless 2026-07-28 spec, Linux Foundation governance, vendor support and the six security risks to plan for.
- [LangGraph in Production: State, Checkpointing and the Failure Modes Nobody Warns You About](https://fwdpod.com/insights/langgraph-in-production): Running LangGraph in production: Postgres checkpointers and the exit, async and sync durability modes, human-in-the-loop interrupts and why nodes re-run on resume, retry and timeout policies, streaming and double texting, LangSmith tracing, tests and trajectory evals, deployment options, a readiness checklist and questions for hiring LangGraph developers.
- [Data Security in Offshore AI Development: The 12 Controls to Demand in Writing](https://fwdpod.com/insights/data-security-offshore-ai-development): Twelve contract-ready data security controls for offshore AI teams, from client-owned cloud and model accounts, SSO and masked data to LLM provider retention settings, prompt and trace handling, secrets, DLP for AI tools, offboarding, incident windows and subprocessor approval, each mapped to ISO 27001 Annex A, NIST SP 800-53 and the OWASP LLM Top 10.
- [Forward Deployed Engineer vs Solutions Engineer: Where the Line Actually Sits](https://fwdpod.com/insights/fde-vs-solutions-engineer): How forward deployed engineers and solutions engineers differ on deal stage, reporting line, output and success metric, where the roles blur, how sales engineers, solutions architects and customer success engineers compare, and which one a buyer should ask a vendor for.
- [When to Hire a Forward Deployed Engineer (and When You Genuinely Do Not Need One)](https://fwdpod.com/insights/when-to-hire-a-forward-deployed-engineer): Seven signals that call for a forward deployed engineer, five signs you do not need one, which alternative fits each situation (SaaS, readiness assessment, staff augmentation, an AI pod or in-house hiring), what must be in place before an FDE starts, and three timing mistakes.
- [How to Choose a Forward Deployed Engineering Company: Nine Questions That Separate Them](https://fwdpod.com/insights/choosing-a-forward-deployed-engineering-company): Nine questions for comparing forward deployed engineering vendors (who is embedded, production ownership, access limits, handover, time-zone overlap, IP in prompts and eval sets, exit, evals and the commercial model), with good and red-flag answers and a weighted scorecard.
